_meta.description: KSP Trinetra Sentinel — IPC to BNS 2023 Legal Knowledge Base Seed Corpus
_meta.assistive_note: All entries are ASSISTIVE ONLY. Officers must independently verify all elements before applying any section.
_meta.source: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, Indian Penal Code 1860, NDPS Act 1985, POCSO Act 2012

mappings.offence_title: Punishment for Murder
mappings.max_punishment: Death or Imprisonment for Life + Fine
elements: Unlawful killing of a human being
Intention to cause death
OR intention to cause bodily injury sufficient to cause death in ordinary nature

ingredient_checklist.item: Victim is a human being
Death of victim established (medical / forensic)
Accused caused the act leading to death
Mens rea: intent to kill or cause grievous injury
No exception applies (grave provocation, right of private defence, etc.)

mappings.key_case_law: State of UP v. Sri Krishna (1976) — distinction between murder and culpable homicide not amounting to murder

mappings.offence_title: Culpable Homicide Not Amounting to Murder
mappings.max_punishment: 10 years imprisonment + Fine (Part I) / 7 years (Part II)
elements: Causing death of a person
Without intent to cause death (distinguished from murder)
Knowledge that act is likely to cause death

ingredient_checklist.item: Death of victim established
Act of accused caused death
No premeditated intention to kill (distinguishes from BNS 101)
Knowledge of likelihood of death

mappings.key_case_law: Jagrup Singh v. State of Haryana (1981)

mappings.offence_title: Attempt to Murder
mappings.max_punishment: 10 years imprisonment + Fine; Life if victim grievously hurt
elements: Act done with intention to commit murder
Act capable of causing death if not prevented
Victim need not die

ingredient_checklist.item: Clear intention to kill established
Overt act committed toward killing
Act goes beyond mere preparation

mappings.key_case_law: Om Prakash v. State of Punjab (1961)

mappings.offence_title: Rape / Sexual Assault
mappings.max_punishment: Minimum 10 years to Life + Fine (Rigorous Imprisonment)
elements: Sexual penetration without consent
OR with consent obtained through coercion, fraud, or impersonation
Includes digital penetration and use of objects

ingredient_checklist.item: Medical examination report obtained
Survivor statement recorded (Section 164 CrPC/BNSS)
Absence of consent established
POCSO sections added if survivor is a minor
DNA/forensic evidence collected within 72 hours

mappings.key_case_law: Tukaram v. State of Maharashtra (1979); Lillu @ Rajesh v. State of Haryana (2013)

mappings.offence_title: Assault or Criminal Force Against Woman with Intent to Outrage Modesty
elements: Use of assault or criminal force
Against a woman
With intent to outrage her modesty

ingredient_checklist.item: Complainant is a woman
Act involved physical contact or threatening gesture
Intent to outrage modesty demonstrable

mappings.key_case_law: Ramkripal v. State of MP (2007)

mappings.offence_title: Theft
elements: Dishonest intention to take moveable property
Property taken out of possession of another without consent

ingredient_checklist.item: Property is moveable
Property was in possession of another person
Taken without consent of possessor
Dishonest intent at time of taking

mappings.key_case_law: Pyarelal Bhargava v. State of Rajasthan (1963)

mappings.offence_title: Theft in Dwelling House
elements: Theft committed in a dwelling house, tent, or vessel
Used as a human dwelling or custody of property

ingredient_checklist.item: All elements of BNS 303 (Theft) established
Location is a dwelling house or equivalent
Entry into premises established

mappings.key_case_law: Madhu v. State of Kerala (2012)

mappings.offence_title: Robbery
mappings.max_punishment: 10 years imprisonment + Fine; 14 years if highway robbery
elements: Theft or extortion accompanied by use of force / threat of force
Violence or threat at time of commission or for carrying away property

ingredient_checklist.item: Theft elements established (BNS 303)
Force/threat used voluntarily before or during the theft
Victim put in fear of instant death, hurt, or wrongful restraint

mappings.key_case_law: Om Prakash v. State of Rajasthan (1997)

mappings.offence_title: Dacoity
elements: Robbery committed by 5 or more persons
All persons present (even those not directly committing robbery are liable)

ingredient_checklist.item: Robbery elements established (BNS 309)
5 or more persons involved and present
Common intention to commit robbery

mappings.key_case_law: Bhagwan Singh v. State of MP (2002)

mappings.offence_title: Robbery or Dacoity with Attempt to Cause Death or Grievous Hurt
elements: Robbery or Dacoity committed
Deadly weapon used OR grievous hurt caused OR attempt to cause death

ingredient_checklist.item: Robbery or Dacoity elements established
Deadly weapon (knife, firearm, etc.) used or carried
Victim suffered grievous hurt OR death was attempted

mappings.key_case_law: Shambhu Nath Singh v. State of Bihar (1960)

mappings.offence_title: Criminal Breach of Trust
elements: Entrustment of property
Dishonest misappropriation or conversion to own use
OR dishonest disposal/use in violation of trust

ingredient_checklist.item: Property was entrusted to accused
Entrustment documented (receipt, contract, ledger)
Misappropriation or breach established
Dishonest intent proven

mappings.key_case_law: Velji Raghavji Patel v. State of Maharashtra (1965)

mappings.offence_title: Cheating and Dishonestly Inducing Delivery of Property
elements: Deception of a person
Fraudulently or dishonestly inducing the deceived person to deliver property
OR to consent to retention of property by any person
OR to alter or destroy signed/valuable security

ingredient_checklist.item: Deception / fraudulent misrepresentation established
Victim induced to deliver property or sign document
Accused received property or benefit
Dishonest intent at time of deception
Cyber Cell freeze requested if UPI/bank transactions involved

mappings.key_case_law: Hridaya Ranjan Prasad Verma v. State of Bihar (2000); Vesa Holdings v. State of Kerala (2015)

mappings.offence_title: Criminal Trespass
elements: Entry into property in possession of another
With intent to commit offence, intimidate, insult, or annoy

ingredient_checklist.item: Property is in possession of complainant
Entry by accused established
Intent to commit offence or annoy established

mappings.key_case_law: Mathai v. State of Kerala (2005)

mappings.offence_title: House Trespass
elements: Criminal trespass committed in a building / dwelling house / vessel

ingredient_checklist.item: All elements of BNS 329 (Criminal Trespass) established
Location is a building, tent, or vessel used as dwelling or property custody

mappings.key_case_law: Biswabhusan Naik v. State of Orissa (1954)

mappings.offence_title: House Trespass for Committing Offence Punishable with Imprisonment
elements: House Trespass
With intent to commit any offence punishable with imprisonment

ingredient_checklist.item: House trespass elements established (BNS 330)
Intent to commit imprisonable offence inside

mappings.key_case_law: Kishori Lal v. State of UP (1981)

mappings.offence_title: Lurking House Trespass or House Breaking by Night
elements: House trespass
Committed after sunset and before sunrise (nighttime)
OR by lurking (concealing presence)

ingredient_checklist.item: House trespass elements established
Time of trespass was after sunset / before sunrise
Method of entry involved breaking or concealment

mappings.key_case_law: State of Rajasthan v. Mohan Lal (1979)

mappings.offence_title: Voluntarily Causing Hurt
mappings.max_punishment: 1 year imprisonment + Fine of Rs 1000, or both
elements: Voluntarily causing hurt to another person
Without lawful excuse

ingredient_checklist.item: Physical injury, pain, disease, or infirmity caused
Act was voluntary (not accidental)
Medical certificate obtained

mappings.key_case_law: State of Karnataka v. Suresh (2001)

mappings.offence_title: Voluntarily Causing Hurt by Dangerous Weapons or Means
elements: Hurt caused by shooting, stabbing, cutting
OR use of fire, heated substance, poison, corrosive substance, explosive

ingredient_checklist.item: Hurt established (BNS 115 elements)
Weapon or dangerous means used is documented (seized)
Weapon capable of causing death

mappings.key_case_law: Rajinder Kumar v. State of UP (2007)

mappings.offence_title: Voluntarily Causing Grievous Hurt by Dangerous Weapons
mappings.max_punishment: Life Imprisonment + Fine, or Imprisonment up to 10 years + Fine
elements: Grievous hurt caused by dangerous weapon or means
Voluntary act with intent or knowledge

ingredient_checklist.item: Grievous hurt established (permanent disability, dangerous limb injury, etc.)
Weapon / dangerous means used
Medical report specifying nature of grievous injury

mappings.key_case_law: State of UP v. Ram Swarup (1974)

mappings.offence_title: Wrongful Restraint
mappings.max_punishment: 1 month imprisonment + Fine of Rs 500, or both
elements: Voluntarily obstructs a person
Preventing from proceeding in a direction the person has right to proceed

ingredient_checklist.item: Obstruction was physical or by show of force
Person was prevented from exercising legal right of movement

mappings.key_case_law: State v. Dharam Pal (1975)

mappings.offence_title: Wrongful Confinement
mappings.max_punishment: 1 year imprisonment + Fine of Rs 1000, or both
elements: Wrongful restraint in all directions (not just one)
Unlawful detention of a person

ingredient_checklist.item: Person was confined in a bounded space
Detention was without legal authority
Duration of confinement established

mappings.key_case_law: Bhim Singh v. State of J&K (1985)

mappings.offence_title: Kidnapping
elements: Taking or enticing away a person from lawful guardianship
Without consent of guardian (for minors)
OR by force / deceit (for adults)

ingredient_checklist.item: Victim is a minor (under 16 for males / 18 for females) OR adult taken by force
Removal from lawful guardianship established
Consent of guardian (if minor) was not obtained
POCSO Act applicable if victim is a child

mappings.key_case_law: State v. Sanjay Kumar (2020)

mappings.offence_title: Kidnapping or Abduction for Murder
elements: Kidnapping or abduction
With intent that victim be murdered or put in danger of being murdered

ingredient_checklist.item: Kidnapping elements established (BNS 137)
Intent to murder or expose to danger of murder

mappings.key_case_law: Prabhu Babaji Navle v. State of Bombay (1956)

mappings.offence_title: Cruelty by Husband or Relatives (Domestic Violence)
elements: Husband or relative of husband
Subjects a woman to cruelty
Cruelty = wilful conduct driving to suicide / grave injury OR harassment for dowry

ingredient_checklist.item: Victim is married woman
Accused is husband or husband's relative
Acts of cruelty (physical/mental/economic) documented
Domestic Incident Report filed under Protection of Women from DV Act 2005

mappings.key_case_law: Sushil Kumar Sharma v. Union of India (2005)

mappings.offence_title: Dowry Death
elements: Death of woman within 7 years of marriage by burns, bodily injury, or in suspicious circumstances
Woman subjected to cruelty or harassment for dowry demands soon before death

ingredient_checklist.item: Death occurred within 7 years of marriage
Circumstances of death are suspicious (not natural)
Evidence of dowry demands / harassment before death
Panchnama and forensic report obtained
Section 113B Evidence Act presumption applicable

mappings.key_case_law: Shanti v. State of Haryana (1991)

mappings.offence_title: Word, Gesture, or Act Intended to Insult the Modesty of a Woman
elements: Word, sound, or gesture made
With intention of insulting modesty of a woman
Intrudes upon privacy of a woman

ingredient_checklist.item: Act/word/gesture directed at a woman
Intent to insult modesty established
Victim's statement recorded

mappings.key_case_law: Rupan Deol Bajaj v. KPS Gill (1995)

mappings.offence_title: Promoting Enmity Between Groups on Grounds of Religion, Race, Caste, etc.
mappings.max_punishment: 3 years imprisonment + Fine; 5 years if at place of worship
elements: Words, signs, visible representations
Promoting disharmony or feelings of enmity between groups

ingredient_checklist.item: Specific words/content promoting enmity identified and documented
Target group identifiable by religion, race, caste, language, etc.
Content likely to cause public disorder

mappings.key_case_law: Balwant Singh v. State of Punjab (1995)

mappings.offence_title: Obstructing Public Servant in Discharge of Public Functions
mappings.max_punishment: 3 months imprisonment + Fine of Rs 500, or both
elements: Voluntarily obstructs a public servant
Obstruction is in discharge of public functions

ingredient_checklist.item: Complainant is a public servant acting in official capacity
Obstruction was voluntary (not inadvertent)
Function being obstructed was lawful

mappings.key_case_law: Biswabhusan Naik v. State (1954)

mappings.offence_title: Assault or Criminal Force to Deter a Public Servant from Discharge of Duty
elements: Assault or criminal force used
Against a public servant
With intent to prevent or deter from performing duties

ingredient_checklist.item: Victim is a public servant on duty
Assault or use of force established
Medical certificate for injuries (if any)
FIR report of on-duty officer (GD entry)

mappings.key_case_law: State of AP v. N. Venugopal (1964)

mappings.offence_title: False Information to Public Servant
mappings.max_punishment: 6 months imprisonment + Fine of Rs 1000, or both
elements: Giving false information to public servant
Intending to cause such servant to use lawful power to injure another

ingredient_checklist.item: Information given was false and known to be so
Information given to a public servant
Intent to cause wrongful injury to another through the servant

mappings.key_case_law: Jagannath v. Emperor (1909)

mappings.offence_title: Criminal Conspiracy
mappings.max_punishment: Same as substantive offence conspired to commit; up to 6 months if minor offence
elements: Agreement between 2 or more persons
To commit an illegal act or legal act by illegal means

ingredient_checklist.item: 2 or more persons involved
Agreement to commit illegal act established
Overt act done in furtherance of conspiracy (for minor offences)
Communication records / CDRs documenting conspiracy

mappings.key_case_law: Mohd. Khalid v. State of West Bengal (2002)

mappings.offence_title: Acts Done by Several Persons in Furtherance of Common Intention
elements: Criminal act done by several persons
In furtherance of common intention of all

ingredient_checklist.item: Common intention shared by all co-accused established
Each accused was present at scene of crime
Each accused participated in the criminal act

mappings.key_case_law: Mahboob Shah v. Emperor (1945)

mappings.offence_title: Rash Driving or Riding on Public Way
mappings.max_punishment: 6 months imprisonment + Fine of Rs 1000, or both
elements: Drives or rides on public way
In manner so rash or negligent as to endanger life

ingredient_checklist.item: Occurrence on public road established
Rash or negligent driving manner documented (speed, video)
Life or limb of others endangered

mappings.key_case_law: Rattan Singh v. State of Punjab (1980)

mappings.offence_title: Causing Death by Negligence
mappings.max_punishment: 2 years imprisonment + Fine, or both; 5 years for hit-and-run (new BNS provision)
elements: Death caused by rash or negligent act
Not amounting to culpable homicide

ingredient_checklist.item: Death of victim established (post-mortem)
Act of accused was the proximate cause of death
Act was rash or negligent (not intentional)
For hit-and-run: accused fled scene (attracts 5-year provision under BNS)

mappings.key_case_law: Jacob Mathew v. State of Punjab (2005) — medical negligence; Alister v. State of Maharashtra (1966)

mappings.offence_title: Forgery
elements: Making a false document or false electronic record
Intent to cause damage or injury / to support a claim / to commit fraud

ingredient_checklist.item: False document / e-record identified and seized
Forgery established through expert examination (handwriting / digital forensics)
Intent to deceive established
Victim or institution affected identified

mappings.key_case_law: State of Bihar v. Om Prakash (1991)

mappings.offence_title: Forgery for Purpose of Cheating
elements: Forgery committed
For the purpose of cheating

ingredient_checklist.item: Forgery established (BNS 336A elements)
Purpose of forgery was to cheat another person
Cheating (BNS 318) also established

mappings.key_case_law: Sheetal Prasad Dixit v. State of UP (1999)

mappings.offence_title: Using as Genuine a Forged Document
elements: Uses a forged document or electronic record
As if it were genuine
Knowing or having reason to believe it is forged

ingredient_checklist.item: Document established as forged (BNS 336A)
Accused used the document as genuine
Knowledge of forgery at time of use established

mappings.key_case_law: Ram Narayan Popli v. CBI (2003)

mappings.offence_title: Counterfeiting Currency Notes or Bank Notes
elements: Counterfeiting of currency note or bank note
Knowledge that it is a counterfeit

ingredient_checklist.item: Fake currency notes seized and sent for forensic examination
RBI / currency expert report confirming counterfeiting
Accused in possession of / producing counterfeit notes
FICN database cross-check conducted

mappings.key_case_law: Superintendent of Police v. Dinakar (2008)

mappings.offence_title: Possession, Sale, Purchase of Manufactured Drugs (NDPS Act)
mappings.max_punishment: 10 years to Life Imprisonment + Fine (based on quantity: small / commercial)
elements: Possession, sale, purchase, transport, use of manufactured drugs
Without lawful authority

ingredient_checklist.item: Drug seized and sent for chemical analysis
CFSL / FSL report confirming drug nature
Quantity determined (small / intermediate / commercial)
Section 50 NDPS compliance (search in presence of gazetted officer / magistrate)
Accused offered option of Magistrate for search

mappings.key_case_law: State of Punjab v. Baljinder Singh (2019) — Section 50 compliance mandatory

mappings.offence_title: Identity Theft (IT Act 2000)
mappings.max_punishment: 3 years imprisonment + Fine up to Rs 1 Lakh
elements: Fraudulent or dishonest use of electronic signature, password, or other unique identification feature of another person

ingredient_checklist.item: Electronic identity credential (OTP, password, UPI PIN) used without authorisation
Digital forensic evidence (device, IP, transaction logs) collected
Victim's loss documented
Cyber Cell FIR filed and 1930 reported
Bank account freeze requested if financial fraud involved

mappings.key_case_law: Vinod Kumar v. State of Haryana (2015)

mappings.offence_title: Cheating by Personation Using Computer Resources (IT Act)
mappings.max_punishment: 3 years imprisonment + Fine up to Rs 1 Lakh
elements: Cheating by personating another person using computer resources or communication device

ingredient_checklist.item: Accused impersonated another through digital means
Communication device / computer resource identified
Fraudulent intent established
Apply BNS 318 (Cheating) in addition if property obtained

mappings.key_case_law: Avnish Bajaj v. State (2005)

mappings.offence_title: Member of Unlawful Assembly
elements: Member of an unlawful assembly (5 or more persons)
Assembly with common object to commit offence / resist legal process

ingredient_checklist.item: Assembly of 5 or more persons established
Common unlawful object identified
Accused was a member of the assembly

mappings.key_case_law: Masalti v. State of UP (1964)

mappings.offence_title: Rioting
elements: Unlawful assembly
Use of force or violence by members
In prosecution of common object

ingredient_checklist.item: Unlawful assembly established (BNS 189)
Force or violence used by assembly members
Accused actively participated (not merely present)
Video/CCTV evidence of violence obtained

mappings.key_case_law: Moti Das v. State of Bihar (1954)

mappings.offence_title: Rioting with Deadly Weapon
elements: Rioting
Armed with deadly weapon / anything used as weapon for causing death

ingredient_checklist.item: Rioting elements established (BNS 191)
Deadly weapon carried / used by accused
Weapon seized and documented in panchnama

mappings.key_case_law: State of UP v. Sughar Singh (1978)

mappings.offence_title: Causing Disappearance of Evidence / Giving False Information to Screen Offender
mappings.max_punishment: Same as principal offence (max 7 years if murder)
elements: Causes any evidence to disappear
OR gives false information to screen any offender from legal punishment

ingredient_checklist.item: Evidence was deliberately destroyed or concealed
Accused knew of commission of the principal offence
Intent to screen the offender from legal punishment

mappings.key_case_law: Gura Singh v. State of Rajasthan (2001)

mappings.offence_title: Dishonestly Receiving Stolen Property
elements: Dishonestly receives or retains stolen property
Having reason to believe it to be stolen

ingredient_checklist.item: Property established as stolen (linked FIR)
Property found in possession of accused
Accused had reason to believe property was stolen

mappings.key_case_law: State v. Mohan Lal (1989)

mappings.offence_title: Defamation
elements: Makes or publishes any imputation concerning a person
With intent to harm or knowledge that harm will be caused to reputation

ingredient_checklist.item: Imputation is about a specific identifiable person
Imputation is false and published to third parties
Harm to reputation established
None of the defamation exceptions apply (truth for public good, fair comment, etc.)

mappings.key_case_law: Subramanian Swamy v. Union of India (2016)

mappings.offence_title: Penetrative Sexual Assault on Child (POCSO Act 2012)
mappings.max_punishment: Minimum 10 years Rigorous Imprisonment to Life + Fine
elements: Penetrative sexual assault
Committed against a child (under 18 years)

ingredient_checklist.item: Victim is under 18 years of age (birth certificate / school records)
Medical examination of child conducted by qualified doctor
Child's statement recorded before Magistrate (Section 164 CrPC)
Special Court / POCSO Court intimated
Child Welfare Committee (CWC) notified
CCTV/VCD recording of statement if possible

mappings.key_case_law: Independent Thought v. Union of India (2017)

mappings.offence_title: Obscene Acts and Songs in Public Places
elements: Obscene act in public place to annoyance of others
OR singing / reciting obscene songs in public

ingredient_checklist.item: Act occurred in a public place
Act caused annoyance to persons present
Nature of act is obscene (not merely indecent)

mappings.key_case_law: Ranjit D. Udeshi v. State of Maharashtra (1964)

mappings.offence_title: Attempt to Commit Culpable Homicide Not Amounting to Murder
mappings.max_punishment: 3 years + Fine if no hurt; 7 years + Fine if hurt caused
elements: Act done with intention of committing culpable homicide
Act not amounting to attempt to murder

ingredient_checklist.item: Intention to cause death (but not premeditated murder intent)
Overt act toward causing death
Distinguished from BNS 109 (Attempt to Murder)

mappings.key_case_law: State of Karnataka v. Razak Khan (1996)

mappings.offence_title: Disobedience to Order Duly Promulgated by Public Servant
mappings.max_punishment: 1 month to 6 months imprisonment + Fine (if danger to human life)
elements: Order lawfully promulgated by public servant
Accused knowingly disobeys
Obstruction, annoyance, or injury to legally employed persons results

ingredient_checklist.item: Order is lawfully promulgated and published (Section 144 CrPC / BNSS)
Accused had knowledge of the order
Disobedience caused/likely to cause obstruction or injury

mappings.key_case_law: Babulal Parate v. State of Maharashtra (1960)

mappings.offence_title: Mischief Causing Damage to Property (Rs 50 or above)
elements: Destroys or diminishes value of property
Damage amount Rs 50 or more

ingredient_checklist.item: Property damage established through valuation
Damage amount exceeds Rs 50 (Rs 10,000 in practice for FIR)
Accused caused the damage intentionally

mappings.key_case_law: State of Rajasthan v. Gopal Lal (1979)

mappings.offence_title: Mischief by Fire or Explosive Substance to Destroy House, etc.
elements: Commits mischief by fire or explosive substance
Destroys or damages a building used as dwelling / worship / custody of property

ingredient_checklist.item: Fire or explosion established as the cause of damage
Building used as dwelling, worship, or property custody
Accused intentionally set the fire / caused explosion
Forensic fire investigation report obtained

mappings.key_case_law: State of Maharashtra v. Sarfaraz (2001)

mappings.offence_title: Statements Conducing to Public Mischief
mappings.max_punishment: 2 years imprisonment + Fine; 5 years if communal disharmony provoked
elements: Makes, publishes, or circulates statements
With intent or likelihood of causing fear, alarm, incitement to offence

ingredient_checklist.item: Statement / publication identified and preserved
Intent to cause public mischief or alarm established
Statements targeted specific community (if communal charges)

mappings.key_case_law: Kedar Nath Singh v. State of Bihar (1962)

mappings.offence_title: Abettor Present When Offence is Committed
elements: Person abets the commission of an offence
Is present at time of commission of offence

ingredient_checklist.item: Abetment established (instigation / conspiracy / assistance)
Accused was physically present at scene of crime
Principal offence was committed

mappings.key_case_law: Dhananjaya Reddy v. State of Karnataka (2001)

mappings.offence_title: Abetment of a Thing
elements: Instigates any person to commit an offence
OR engages in a conspiracy for commission of offence
OR intentionally aids commission

ingredient_checklist.item: Mode of abetment (instigation / conspiracy / aiding) clearly established
Principal offence was committed (or attempted)
Nexus between abettor and principal offence demonstrated

mappings.key_case_law: Som Nath Thapa v. State of Maharashtra (1996)

mappings.offence_title: Illegal Possession / Use of Arms (Arms Act 1959)
mappings.max_punishment: 3 years to Life Imprisonment (based on nature of arm)
elements: Possession, use, manufacture of arms / ammunition
Without valid licence or in contravention of Arms Act

ingredient_checklist.item: Arm / ammunition seized and sent for ballistic examination
No valid licence exists for accused
Ballistics report confirming weapon nature (country-made / licensed type)
FSL report on operational status of firearm

mappings.key_case_law: State of Karnataka v. Yadavappa (2009)

mappings.offence_title: Non-Appearance in Response to Proclamation under Section 82 CrPC
mappings.max_punishment: 3 years imprisonment + Fine; 7 years if offence is punishable with life/death
elements: Person fails to appear at specified place/time after proclamation
Proclamation issued under Section 82 CrPC / BNSS

ingredient_checklist.item: Proclamation under Section 82 CrPC / Section 84 BNSS issued and served
Period of 30 days elapsed since proclamation
Accused failed to appear as directed
Gazette publication / beat-level notice documented

mappings.key_case_law: Sube Singh v. State of Haryana (2006)
